authority: Caledonian MacBrayne (CalMac) — Scottish Government lifeline ferry network
operator_note: CalMac operates Scotland's west-coast lifeline ferry network under contract to Transport Scotland (Scottish Government), via CMAL-owned vessels/harbours. Stakeholder = Transport Scotland / CalMac. Public lifeline transport authority.
seed_node_coords_source: Firth of Clyde open water (Clyde gateway cluster hub between Ardrossan, Wemyss Bay, Gourock and the inner isles). Mint on water. Retrieved 2026-07-02.
scope_note: CalMac spans 30+ routes across the Clyde and Hebrides — too broad to seal wholesale. Phase D anchors the DOMESTIC-FIRST high-frequency Clyde gateway crossings (busiest, most commuter-like). Outer Hebrides long-haul lifeline legs are noted for a later horizon, not sealed now.
decarbonization_anchor: Scotland targets net zero by 2045; CMAL/CalMac fleet renewal includes new dual-fuel and electric-hybrid vessels (e.g. Glen Sannox LNG/battery on the Arran run). A zero-emission foiling tier fits the fleet-renewal mandate on the shorter, high-frequency Clyde crossings.
network_reality: 34 vessels, 50+ ports. Busiest/most-commuter crossings sit on the Firth of Clyde. Ardrossan/Troon <-> Brodick (Arran) is the single busiest route; Wemyss Bay <-> Rothesay (Bute) and Gourock <-> Dunoon (Cowal) are high-frequency short gateway crossings. Oban <-> Craignure (Mull) anchors the Argyll gateway.

corridors.name: Oban <-> Craignure
corridors.note: Argyll gateway to Mull — later horizon

geometry_note: Open-water Firth of Clyde / Sound of Mull crossings; hand-waypoint around headlands and harbour approaches; no land crossings. Domestic-first: seal the Clyde gateway crossings; hold Outer Hebrides long-haul for a later horizon.
atlas_warning: ALL existing atlas hits for CalMac/Scottish ports are mis-geocoded junk (Tacloban Harbour -> Philippines; Otrobanda/Willemstad -> Curacao). Do NOT bind any. Greenfield mint only.
provenance: calmac.co.uk route-information (Wemyss Bay-Rothesay, Gourock-Dunoon); directferries CalMac (12+ island routes); community sourcing (Ardrossan-Brodick busiest; 34 vessels 50+ ports). Glen Sannox LNG/battery public record. Retrieved 2026-07-02.
